courier-relay/protocol-selection: Courier Relay protocol selection: an omitted "protocol" key selects the current protocol version (constant CURRENT_PROTOCOL in main.py, "2" as of 2026-09-07 after trial-1mb; it was "1" before that). An explicit supported version selects that version; protocol "1" remains supported explicitly for count, summary, and accepted, and keeps its original contract ((account_id, delivery_id) identity, earliest occurred_at UTC instant wins, ties on smallest record_id). Protocol "2" — adopted permanently by the provider and approved by the integration owner as current in trial-1mb — identifies a delivery by delivery_id alone across all accounts, accepts the receipt with the latest occurred_at UTC instant (ties on smallest record_id), and presents accepted receipts in input order with original fields and timestamp spelling. A known command with an explicit unsupported/unknown protocol version returns {"error":"unknown_protocol"}; unknown commands still return {"error":"unknown_command"} regardless of protocol. Protocol handlers are dispatched via PROTOCOLS in main.py: command -> version -> handler. Decided while implementing trial-gbn (count, protocol 1), revised in trial-1mb (protocol 2 current), and in trial-0dq (accepted extended to protocol 1); future protocol-version issues should keep both error shapes stable. The accepted command (added in trial-noq for protocol "2" only, extended to protocol "1" in trial-0dq at the integration partner request, approved) works via the details handler: request {"command":"accepted","receipts":[...]} with optional "protocol" of "1" or "2" returns exactly protocol, accepted_count, duplicate_count, and receipts, where receipts holds that protocol winning representatives unchanged in original input order; its counts equal summary for the same request and protocol. Between trial-noq and trial-0dq accepted rejected protocol "1" with {"error":"unknown_protocol"}.
